# CamCraft MCP tool reference

The server lists 124 tools. The live `tools/list` reply is the authority; this file is generated from the same table. An argument with `?` is optional.

| Tool | Arguments | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `open_project` | `path`, `read_only?` | Open a .camproj project file, replacing the current document and clearing undo history. With read_only: true, save_project does not write over this file; give it a different path to write a copy, which also ends read-only. |
| `save_project` | `overwrite?`, `path?` | Save the document as a .camproj file. Without a path, saves over the file last opened or saved. If that file on disk changed after this session opened or saved it, the save is refused by name; overwrite: true replaces the file. Refused for the file of a project open read-only: give a different path. |
| `import_model` | `facet_budget?`, `name?`, `path`, `units?` | Import a mesh model (STL, STEP or OBJ) through the app's importers. A name already used by a model updates that model. A STEP model too large to import at full detail, or one whose file's edges lie off their surfaces, answers with reduced_fidelity: how closely its surfaces are approximated, in mm - gouge checks against it are stricter, and its operations are refused at the post when it is too coarse to check; import it again with a larger facet_budget, or export the file again with a tighter tolerance, to clear that. A STEP closed shell that meshes open imports incomplete: reduced_fidelity then says incomplete and names the hole, and every operation on the model is refused at the post. notes lists what the importer changed, e.g. a STEP face wound against its neighbours that was flipped, by name, or a closed STEP solid wound inward that was turned outward; for a STEP file it also states the length unit the model was read in. A STEP file that states no length unit is refused until units gives one. |
| `get_job` | `summary?` | The whole document as JSON: setups (each with model_reference: a solid part, or the virtual reference of its placed DXF profiles), stock, work offsets, models (one imported at reduced fidelity carries reduced_fidelity), DXF profiles, tools, and operations with their parameters and status (one on a DXF profile says what it checks against). With summary, a short form for a small context window: no machine definition, and each operation lists only the fields changed from its defaults. |
| `get_selection` | - | Read currently selected entities, active setup, active operation, viewport pick mode (model, face, edge, vertex), and active geometry picks. |
| `list_operation_types` | `kind?`, `section?` | Every operation kind with its parameter fields, JSON types and default values, and the tool kinds it accepts. kind or section lists only those kinds. |
| `list_tool_catalog` | - | The built-in tool catalog: names and definitions add_tool can copy into the document. |
| `list_holder_library` | - | The built-in holder library: BT30, BT40 and CAT40 holders with ER collet or Weldon side-lock noses, and standalone ER11-ER40 chucks - names set_tool_holder takes, with their dimensions and the shanks they clamp. |
| `set_tool_holder` | `clear?`, `gauge_len?`, `library?`, `points?`, `projection?`, `tool` | Set a document tool's holder: from the holder library by name (optional gauge_len and projection, mm; the tool stores the reference to the entry, shown as holder.library, not a copy of its outline), from a drawn spun profile (points; a custom holder), or back to the holder cylinder (clear). One undo step; an unknown entry, a shank the holder cannot take or a bad profile is refused by name. |
| `add_tool` | `catalog?`, `definition?`, `holder?`, `name?` | Add a tool to the document, from the catalog by name or from a full definition (the shape get_job shows). Assigns the lowest unused tool number in 1-99999 that the mounted machine does not reserve (a probe takes the machine's reserved probe pocket; a cutter on a reserved number or name is refused) and starts with the machine's default holder unless "holder" says otherwise; one undo removes the tool and its holder. A form mill (kind "form_mill") states "form": a "preset" (kind roundover, cove, ogee, v_groove or bead, with its numbers) or drawn "points" [z, r, arc] from the tip up, and "pilot_len" (the non-cutting bearing at the tip); the preset writes the points, and the outline sets diameter and flute_len. No operation cuts with a form mill yet. |
| `edit_tool` | `name`, `patch` | Edit a document tool: "patch" is a partial tool definition (the shape add_tool's definition and get_job show, JSON merge patch - null removes an optional key). It runs the app's undoable ChangeTool, one undo step, so every gate applies (a retype that strands an operation, bad cutting_data rows, catalog values) and refuses by tool name. An unknown key is refused by name. Operations using the tool go stale. A form mill (kind "form_mill") states "form": a "preset" (kind roundover, cove, ogee, v_groove or bead, with its numbers) or drawn "points" [z, r, arc] from the tip up, and "pilot_len" (the non-cutting bearing at the tip); the preset writes the points, and the outline sets diameter and flute_len. No operation cuts with a form mill yet. |
| `delete_tool` | `name` | Delete a document tool through the app's undoable DeleteTool, one undo step (undo restores it with its number, holder body and cutter). Refused by tool name, changing nothing: an unknown name, an entity that is not a tool, or a tool an operation still uses (give that operation another tool with set_tool first). |
| `export_tool_library` | `format?`, `path`, `units?` | Write the document's tools to a CamCraft library (.camtools), a Tormach PathPilot tool table (.csv), or a Hurco WinMax tool library (.TCM), detected from path or chosen with format. units (mm or inch) applies to controller tables and defaults to document units. Refuses a document with no tools, an unwriteable path, or a tool that cannot fit the target table. |
| `import_tool_library` | `format?`, `holders?`, `mode?`, `path`, `units?` | Import a CamCraft library (.camtools/.json), Tormach PathPilot tool table (.csv), or Hurco WinMax tool library (.TCM) as one undo step. format (default auto) overrides detection; units (mm or inch) applies to controller tables and defaults to document units. mode add (default): skips an identical tool, renames a clashing name; update: updates matching names in place; replace: removes absent tools unless used. holders (default true) takes holders from .camtools files. Malformed rows, unsupported Hurco tool types, or tool-number clashes refuse by name. |
| `set_stock` | `angles_deg?`, `axis?`, `box?`, `cylinder?`, `from_model?` | Set the active setup's stock: a box, a cylinder, or a copy of a model, through the undoable SetStock. Optional axis (z, x or y) or angles_deg {yaw, pitch, roll} turns it; the simulation refuses a stock tilted off the axes, by name. |
| `add_operation` | `kind`, `name?`, `params?`, `source?`, `tool?` | Add an operation of a kind (see list_operation_types) with a tool, on the stock, a model or a placed DXF profile (2D milling, plasma, waterjet and wire EDM kinds only; a kind that needs a solid model refuses a profile by name), seeded with the kind's defaults and an optional params patch. Not generated until generate runs. |
| `edit_operation` | `name`, `params` | Patch an operation's parameters: the given fields replace the current ones (JSON merge patch over the kind's fields; null clears an optional field). One undo step. |
| `detect_holes` | `name` | Fill a Drill, Bore or Thread operation's hole list from its source model's holes (the app's Detect holes button); a Thread operation whose params say external: true gets the model's upright round bosses instead. A Bore operation leaves out holes wider than its tool's ring clears without a core (3 x tool diameter + 2 x stock to leave) and names each in `skipped`. A Drill operation keeps a hole wider than its Drill-kind drill (a pilot is valid) and names each in `undersize`; its toolpath then carries a `drill_undersize` warning per such hole that does not hold the post. One undo step. |
| `detect_pockets` | `create?`, `model`, `name?`, `tool?` | A model's recognised pockets and slots (closed or open pockets, straight slots with open, round or square ends): boundary, floor and top Z, depth, tightest inside corner, slot width and open sides. With create, adds the operation that machines one of them (a Pocket over its floor, or a Slot along its centreline). One undo step. |
| `delete_operation` | `name` | Delete an operation and its cached toolpath. |
| `set_tool` | `operation`, `tool` | Assign a document tool to an operation (the tool must suit the operation's kind). |
| `list_features` | `compact?`, `kinds?`, `limit?`, `model` | A model's, fixture's, or DXF profile's pickable features with stable ids: faces, edge chains, welded smooth faces and vertices on models, or sketch chains and layers on DXF profiles, in world coordinates. |
| `get_operation_geometry` | `operation` | What an operation machines: its source (stock, a model, a DXF profile, or picked features), per-chain overrides, its area controls, and what the picks resolve to. |
| `set_operation_geometry` | `operation`, `picks` | Set the features an operation machines (faces, edge chains, loops, or DXF sketch chains and layers with optional per-chain side and direction overrides) by list_features ids. One undo step; undo restores the previous source. |
| `set_operation_area` | `area`, `operation` | Replace an operation's area controls (containment, offset, outer_offset, corner, extension, extra include/exclude boundaries, open boundary). One undo step. |
| `get_operation_do_not_touch` | `operation` | Read an operation's 'Do not touch' protected faces/edges and standoff clearance (mm). |
| `set_operation_do_not_touch` | `clearance?`, `operation`, `picks?` | Set protected faces or edge chains (plus standoff clearance, mm) that 2D Pocket, Trace, 2D Offset, 2D Adaptive, 3D Pocket, Face, 3D Finish and Engrave paths must stay clear of across flutes, shank, and holder. Refuses unsupported operation kinds, vertex picks, and overlap with the machining selection. One undo step. |
| `undo` | - | Undo the last document change. |
| `redo` | - | Redo the last undone change. |
| `generate` | `name?` | Generate toolpaths: one named operation (always regenerated) or, with no name, every operation that is not current when reached in program order, including operations made stale by earlier generations in this call. A refusal stops the call and names the operation. |
| `verify` | `name?` | Verify the job without posting: per-operation status and findings (op, move index, kind, message, whether it blocks the post) plus the program-level post gate. "ok" is true only when the post would write: every operation fresh, the gate passed, and no operation's own warning blocking the post (those operations are listed under "held_by"). |
| `post` | `between_setups?`, `output`, `post?` | Post the program to an NC file through a post processor (a built-in name or a .cps path; default the document's own). Returns the written files, or refuses with the reasons. between_setups chooses what the program does at a setup change (pause by default). |
| `render_stock` | `height?`, `toolpath?`, `view?`, `width?` | Render the program's simulated stock as a PNG (an image content block), painted by deviation class (clean, rest, gouge, unjudged), optionally with the toolpath over it; plus rest and gouge volume and the bounds of the stock and the rest. Generate first. |
| `add_setup` | `datum_from?`, `name?` | Declare a new setup and make it active. With datum_from, it starts as a copy of that setup's stock and WCS placement. The first setup on a document without setups adopts the existing stock and G54. |
| `activate_setup` | `name` | Make a declared setup the active one: where new operations, stock and WCS edits go. |
| `set_operation_setup` | `operation`, `setup` | Move an operation into another declared setup (setup null: the implicit first position). The stamp is kept, so the operation reads ok or stale by the staleness law. One undo step. Refused by name: an unknown operation or setup, a move to where it already is. |
| `delete_setup` | `name` | Delete a declared setup with its private stock and WCS; one undo restores them. Refused by name while an operation still machines in it (move or delete it first) or another setup is placed relative to it. |
| `set_wcs` | `offset?`, `origin?`, `rotation?`, `stock_point?` | Place the active setup's work coordinate system: an absolute origin, or a point of the stock's bounding box (min/center/max per axis) plus an optional offset. Rotation is a unit quaternion [x, y, z, w]; omitted keeps the current one. |
| `set_work_offset` | `index?`, `setup?`, `word?` | Set the work offset the post uses for a declared setup's WCS: index is 1-based (G54-G59 accepted as aliases of 1-6), bounded by the setup's own post - an offset it cannot express is refused by setup name. null clears it (offset 1). Returns index and the post's name for it (word is an alias of name). Moves no origin. |
| `set_program` | `comment?`, `number?` | State the document's program number (1 to 9999: the O-word O0001-O9999) and program comment (the program's name on Heidenhain and SINUMERIK). An omitted key keeps its value; null clears it (O0001 and the machine's name). One undo step. |
| `set_raw_stock_only` | `on` | For a stock made from a model (set_stock from_model): say whether that source model is raw stock only - a casting or blank you cut into, not the finished part - so the post's gouge verdict does not judge it (on), or is judged like every model (off, the default). An operation that machines the model judges it again. One undo step. |
| `load_machine` | `builtin?`, `clear?`, `path?`, `setup?` | Mount a machine: a built-in by name or a .mch file, or clear it. With setup, the machine is that setup's own (clear: the setup follows the document's machine again); without, it is the document's. |
| `set_setup_post` | `post`, `setup?` | Give a declared setup its own post: a built-in post name or a .cps path; null clears it (the setup follows the document's post again). One undo step. This sets the field only - posting judges whether the post serves the setup's machine. |
| `add_fixture` | `model`, `setup?` | Mark an imported model as a fixture (workholding steel the verifier checks every toolpath against) of a setup - the active one by default. Import the model with import_model first. |
| `remove_fixture` | `name` | Unmark a fixture: the model stays, the verifier stops checking against it. |
| `move_fixture` | `name`, `position`, `rotation?` | Place a fixture: position [x, y, z] in mm and an optional unit quaternion rotation [x, y, z, w] (omitted keeps the current one). |
| `locate_part` | `body?`, `fixture`, `mates`, `move?`, `offset?`, `part`, `turn?` | Locate the part in a fixture (or, with move "fixture", the fixture on the part) by mates: each mate pairs a part face or vertex id (or, with body "stock", a face or vertex id of the setup's stock) with the fixture face or vertex it sits on (list_features prints the ids). One to three mates - floor, fixed jaw, stop (3-2-1) - then an optional offset [dx, dy, dz] mm and turn (degrees about the first face mate's normal). One undoable step; refusals and an interpenetration warning are said by name. |
| `get_fixture_findings` | - | The verifier's fixture check, live: every setup's fixtures and machine table with their boxes, and each collision of a toolpath with them (op, move index, struck part, message). Needs every operation generated. |
| `turn_fixture` | `axis`, `degrees`, `name` | Turn a fixture about world axis "x", "y" or "z" through its own origin by "degrees" (90 or -90 for a quarter turn; + is counter-clockwise looking down the axis). Plate riders turn with it; a part or stock it held stays and is named in "warning". The post gate checks toolpaths against the turned fixture. One undo step. |
| `import_dxf_fixture` | `axis?`, `depth?`, `dxf?`, `kind`, `name?`, `path?`, `position?`, `rotation?`, `setup?` | Import a spun (turning) or extruded (milling) fixture from an ASCII DXF file path or inline DXF text. Spun reads CENTRELINE + half-profile; extruded reads a closed profile + depth (from depth arg or DXF DEPTH annotation/layer) extruded along X/Y/Z. One undoable step. |
| `set_fixture_profile` | `name`, `profile` | Replace a profile fixture's spun or extruded profile geometry (regenerating facets immediately in one undoable step). Refuses STEP fixtures that keep STEP as their source. |
| `derive_fixture_profile` | `axis?`, `kind`, `name` | Derive a reference spun or extruded profile from an imported STEP fixture's solid mesh while keeping its STEP source and facets intact. Refused by name for a fixture without a STEP source (a DXF/profile fixture: edit its profile with set_fixture_profile). One undoable step. |
| `get_fixture_profile` | `name` | Read a fixture's profile definition (spun or extruded), whether it keeps a STEP source, and its facet count. |
| `export_fixture_dxf` | `name`, `path?` | Export a profile fixture's spun or extruded outline as ASCII DXF text (optionally writing to path). |
| `align_part_cylinder` | `angle_deg?`, `flip?`, `pick`, `setup?`, `target?` | Align a picked cylinder or bore wall (a list_features patch id) to target x, y or z (default z), then turn angle_deg (default 0) about that axis. flip reverses the wall axis. Uses the GUI's checked alignment command, including its axis landing proof; one undo step. Refuses unknown setups or models, non-cylinder picks, unusable frames and unchanged poses by name. |
| `place_setup_origin` | `pick?`, `point?`, `setup?`, `source` | Place a named setup's WCS origin (default active setup) from source model_box, stock_box or vertex. Boxes take point corner (default) or centre; vertex takes one list_features pick. Keeps the WCS rotation and uses the GUI's undoable command. Refuses missing geometry, invalid picks and unchanged origins by name; one undo step. |
| `set_part_axes` | `flip_x?`, `flip_y?`, `primary?`, `setup?`, `x?`, `y?` | Align the part from picked axes, as the Setups page's "Part axes" rows do. Picks are list_features ids: one edge chain, or two points (first to second) - a point is a vertex id, or the chain id of a circular edge (a hole rim, a boss edge) for its centre; flip_y / flip_x reverse a pick. One axis (+Y or +X): the part turns in the setup's work plane (its XY) so the pick, projected into the plane, runs along that axis (turn_deg reports the turn). Both axes: their 3D directions define the full frame (frame "full_3d") - primary (default "y") lands exactly, the other is made square to it, and +Z lands on the right-hand cross of the picks, so a left-handed pair is honoured literally (the part lands on its head), not refused. The part turns about its bounds' centre, composed onto the setup's current part alignment; the work offset is untouched; one undo step. Refused by name: a face, a curved edge as the one pick, an edge in a point pair that is not circular (straight, or no circle within tolerance), coincident points, a single pick along Z, X and Y picks running (nearly) along each other. |
| `lay_part_on_points` | `flip?`, `frame?`, `place?`, `plane?`, `points`, `setup?` | Lay the part on a setup's G17 (XY), G18 (ZX) or G19 (YZ) plane through three picked points (list_features vertex ids, or the chain id of a circular edge - a hole rim, a boss edge - for its centre). The plane through them is turned so its outside (the side away from the part's material) faces the plane's axis (+Z for G17), or the opposite way with flip (G17 + flip: the points rest on the table, part above), and point 1 is set onto the plane's level (place, default true). frame (3-2-1) also turns the part so point 1 -> 2 runs along +X (+Y for G19) and moves point 1 to the setup origin. Absolute like the face pick; one undo step; the work offset is untouched. Refused by name: not three points, a face, an edge that is not circular (straight, or no circle within tolerance), points closer than 0.001 mm, (nearly) collinear points (under 1 degree of spread), a pick off the part, no model. |
| `lay_part_on_face` | `face`, `flip?`, `place?`, `plane?`, `setup?` | Lay the part on a setup's G17 (XY), G18 (ZX) or G19 (YZ) plane by one picked flat face (a list_features face id, as {model, id}). The face's outward normal is turned to face the plane's axis (+Z for G17), or the opposite way with flip (G17 + flip: the face rests on the table, part above), and the face's centroid is set onto the plane's level (place, default true). Absolute like the face pick on the Setups page; one undo step; the work offset is untouched. Returns the setup, the face's outside, the stored alignment and its description. Refused by name: an edge, a vertex, a curved or degenerate face, more than one face, a pick off the part, no model, and a lay the setup already holds. |
| `set_wcs_circle_centre` | `edge`, `rotation?` | Place the active setup's work coordinate system on the centre of a picked circular edge (a hole rim or a boss edge; a full circle or an arc): one list_features edge chain id. The origin goes to the circle's centre at the edge's height; the result also states the circle's axis and diameter. Rotation is a unit quaternion [x, y, z, w]; omitted keeps the current one. One undo step. Refused by name: a straight edge, a curve that is not circular within tolerance, a run of fewer than three segments, a face or a vertex. |
| `set_operation_coolant` | `coolant`, `name` | Set an operation's coolant: off, flood, mist, air or through-tool. One undo step, the same command the operation page's coolant picker runs. A mode the operation's machine has no coded entry for is still set, with a "warning" (the post refuses it at post time). |
| `set_wcs_from_features` | `picks`, `setup?` | Place the active setup's work coordinate system on a frame fitted to picked features - the GUI's "Set WCS from features". Each pick is a list_features id plus the role it sets: origin, x, y or z. Axes read in Z, X, Y priority: the first axis pick is exact, the second is squared to it, the third axis is derived right-handed (a third axis pick is ignored). A flat face sets its outward normal, a straight edge its direction (sided away from the origin pick), a curved wall (face or patch) its fitted axis; the origin is a vertex, a face's centroid or a wall's centre, else the second axis pick's anchor, projected onto the first pick's plane when that pick is a face. One undo step. Refused by name: fewer than two picks, a role given twice, fewer than two axes, a pick that cannot set its role (a vertex for an axis, an edge for the origin), a curved or zero-length edge, near-parallel axes (under 5 degrees apart), an unfittable wall, a stale feature id, a setup that is not the active one. |
| `set_wcs_flip` | `setup?`, `x?`, `y?`, `z?` | Set which axes of a setup's work coordinate system run reversed (a flip: X+ becomes X-), as the WCS page's Flip X, Flip Y and Flip Z buttons do. Give x, y and/or z as true (flipped) or false (normal); an axis not given keeps its flag. The origin and rotation do not change. One undo step. Toolpaths do not change. The post mirrors the program on a flipped X or Y: coordinate signs, arc direction and cutter compensation side. A Z rotation is carried in Bake and Control modes. The reply's refused field is null when the flip is carried, else it holds why the post refuses it: a flipped Z, a WCS tilted off Z, or a post not verified for a mirrored program (each built-in mill post is). Refused by name: no flag given, a flag that is not a boolean, an unknown setup. |
| `delete_model` | `name` | Delete an imported part through DeleteEntity. One undo step restores it; redo deletes it again. Refused by name without changing history: an unknown name, a non-model, a fixture, or a model still used by an operation (source, selection or area boundary) or from-model stock, including a setup's stock. Remove those references first; remove_fixture unmarks workholding before deletion. |
| `move_model` | `name`, `position`, `rotation?` | Place an imported part: position [x, y, z] in mm and an optional unit quaternion rotation [x, y, z, w] (omitted keeps the current one). Stock made from the part, or the stock of a one-part document, moves with it and is listed under "stock". One undo step. Refused by name: a fixture (move_fixture places it), a work offset (set_wcs), the machine table, an unknown name, a rotation that is not a quaternion. |
| `repair_model` | `max_hole_edges?`, `name`, `weld_tol?` | Repair an imported model's mesh, as the Model page's Repair button does: weld vertices within weld_tol mm (default 0.001), drop collapsed or duplicate triangles, and fill every open boundary loop of at most max_hole_edges edges (default 256). Returns the counts before and after. One undo step that restores the exact previous facets. Refused by name: an unknown name, the setup's stock or work offsets, a negative tolerance, a budget under 3 edges, a mesh the repair can't close (non-manifold, over budget), and a mesh with nothing to repair. |
| `set_model_link` | `model`, `path` | Link a model to a file, or unlink it. A linked model is imported again under the same name when its file changes (a new SHA-256), while the project is open in the app window: one undo step, and its operations go Stale. Nothing is regenerated or posted by itself. Give "path" as a file to link to (its digest is recorded now; the file is not imported), or as null to unlink. An import from a file links the model already. One undo step. Refused by name: an unknown model, a name that is not a model, a file that cannot be read, unlinking a model that is not linked. |
| `vouch_model_fidelity` | `by`, `model` | Vouch for the mesh of a model marked "fidelity unknown" (a model of a project saved before v59, whose reduced_fidelity says fidelity_unknown), so that its operations can post again without a re-import. Use it only when a person states that the mesh is exact or fine enough: gouge checks then read the mesh as exact. "by" names that person; the history and the model page show it. The mark also leaves the stocks copied from the model. One undo step; undo puts the mark back. Refused by name: an unknown model, a name that is not a model, an empty "by", a model that is not marked, a model with a recorded reduced fidelity (import it again with a larger facet_budget), and an incomplete model (walls missing). |
| `add_builtin_vise` | `dimensions?`, `fit_to_stock?`, `opening?`, `position?`, `rotation?`, `setup?`, `size` | Place a built-in generic milling vise (size table: 3-8 in, 100-200 mm jaw widths, and the 5-axis self-centering 52/75/80/125 mm rows) as a fixture of a setup - the active one by default. Either fit it to the setup's stock (standard: fixed jaw on the stock's +Y side, centred in X, floor under the stock, jaws opened to the stock's Y width; self-centering: centred on the stock in X and Y, jaws closed to its Y width within the clamping range; with a grip step - dimensions grip_depth/grip_width, not beside the lip_height/lip_depth dovetail - the stock sits on the step's ledge grip_depth below the jaw top, the frame origin is that ledge and the vise floor sits jaw_height - grip_depth lower) or place its frame (standard: origin = the fixed jaw's clamping face, centred, at the floor, jaws open toward -Y; self-centering: origin = the centre between the jaws at the floor, or at the ledge with a grip step) at a position/rotation with an opening. Optional dimension overrides in mm. One undoable step; nonsense dimensions are refused by name. |
| `set_vise` | `dimensions?`, `from_stock?`, `name`, `opening?` | Change a placed built-in vise: its jaw opening in mm, or from_stock to open the jaws to the setup's stock as the vise stands, and/or dimension overrides in mm. The mesh is regenerated; one undoable step. |
| `add_accessory` | `above?`, `dimensions?`, `fit_to_stock?`, `grip?`, `kind`, `position?`, `rotation?`, `setup?`, `steps?`, `under_stock_in_vise?` | Place a built-in workholding accessory as a fixture of a setup (the active one by default): parallels (a pair), block (1-2-3 block), step_block, strap_clamp (strap, stud and heel block; the toe tip at the frame origin on the table, the strap running +X, its underside at clamp_height), soft_jaw or rotary_subplate (#821: the base plate a 4th axis is bolted to - generic default figures, enter your own; its frame's origin on the first pin bore at the underside, +X toward the second; it lands fixed, then goes on a fixture plate's dowel pair with place_on_plate, and its thickness - with every plate under it - raises the rotary's centerline for the index-swing check; its height over the machine table counts too, the larger winning, so one placed on a plate by position is never judged on its own thickness alone), three_jaw_chuck, four_jaw_chuck or collet_chuck (#1442: a lathe chuck - body, jaws or collet nose - its frame's z = 0 the face the work stands on, +Z the spindle axis out of it, the body below; it turns with the part, so the lathe holder law reads it as revolved steel; #1468: a jaw chuck's `grip` is outside - the jaws close on the work - or inside - they open into its bore, jaw_length running inward from the grip diameter; step_height with step_depth makes stepped jaws, the work sitting on the step). Either at a position/rotation of its frame (z = 0 its underside), or - a chuck only - fit_to_stock: the chuck closes on the setup's round stock (standing on a vertical axis) at its underside, the grip or collet bore set to the stock's diameter (stepped jaws: the stock on the step; an inside grip is refused - place it by position), or - parallels only - under_stock_in_vise: the parallels' height is set so the stock's top stands `above` mm over that built-in vise's jaws, and the vise drops to suit. Optional dimension overrides in mm. One undoable step; nonsense dimensions are refused by name. |
| `set_accessory` | `dimensions?`, `grip?`, `name`, `steps?` | Resize a placed built-in accessory: dimension overrides in mm (steps for a step block; grip - outside or inside - for a jaw chuck). The mesh is regenerated; one undoable step. |
| `get_tool_cutter_profile` | `tool` | A milling tool's cutter, neck and shank as a spun half-outline: points [z, r, arc] from the tip (z = 0, on the axis) up to the shank top, arc = 0 for a straight segment else the signed radius of an arc to the next point (positive bulges away from the axis). "drawn" says whether it is a hand-drawn outline or the one the tool's numbers draw. Turning tools have none (they are not spun profiles). |
| `set_tool_cutter_params` | `neck?`, `params?`, `tool` | Edit a milling tool by the parameters its cutter outline is drawn from - any of diameter, corner_r, tip_angle (drill point / chamfer cone, degrees), flute_len, shank_d, shank_len, tip_diameter (mm) and tip_form (a chamfer mill's tip: "sharp", "flat" or "ball"; a flat tip states tip_diameter, a ball tip its radius as corner_r) - and optionally its neck. A drawn outline is carried onto the new numbers (the tip regenerated from the kind, a drawn neck kept above the new flute top, the shank top moved), so outline and numbers keep agreeing. "neck": {diameter, length} draws a straight neck from the flute top; null drops the drawn outline (back to the numbers' own); omitted keeps whatever is drawn. Every tool-edit and cutter refusal by name. One undoable step for numbers and outline together. |
| `set_tool_cutter_profile` | `points`, `tool` | Set a milling tool's drawn cutter outline (points [z, r, arc] tip-up, closed to the axis at both ends), or clear it with points null (back to the outline its numbers draw). It must agree with the tool's numbers: start at the tip, reach exactly the stated diameter within the flute length, end at flute + shank length, never be wider than the cutter or shank above the flutes, not fold over itself - else refused by name. Toolpaths keep reading the numbers; the collision checks and the simulation read a drawn neck where it is narrower than the stated shank (never wider). One undoable step. |
| `set_work_material` | `material` | State the document's workpiece material (the Cutting data page's pick): material is aluminium_6061, mild_steel, stainless_304, grey_cast_iron, brass, plastics_pom, softwood, hardwood, mdf, plywood, acrylic or hdpe, or null to clear it. Re-stating the current material, or an unknown word, is refused by name. One undoable step. |
| `set_stock_material` | `material` | State the workpiece material of the active setup's stock (#2015): a material word as set_work_material takes, or null to clear it. It picks the row of each tool's cutting data the setup's operations are seeded from (the stock's material, else the document's, else the tool's Unknown row): every operation of the setup takes the feed of a row naming the material and the row's stepdown / stepover, in the same undoable step. Tools' spindle rpm follow the document material. Refused by name with no stock, or when the stock already states it. |
| `suggest_cutting_data` | `operation` | The feeds-and-speeds table's suggestion for an operation's tool on the stated material, as data; writes nothing: material, tool material, cutting speed (m/min), feed per tooth (mm), chip-thinning factor, spindle rpm, feed (mm/min) and the machine clamps applied. Refused by name when no material is stated or the table cannot speak for the tool. |
| `apply_cutting_data` | `operation` | Apply suggest_cutting_data's numbers: the operation's feed and its tool's spindle speed, as one undoable step (the Cutting data page's Apply). Refused by name when no material is stated, the kind has no milling feed, or the operation already runs the suggestion. |
| `get_tool_body` | `tool` | A document tool's modelled body, or body: null when it has none (the holder cylinder is judged). A "spindle" body (milling) states the model direction that is the tool axis, the model origin's height above the tip, and its revolved envelope (foot, top, max_radius above the tip); a "lathe" body states its placement in the turning tool frame (radial, along, tip), its insert zone and its extent from the tip (radial, normal, spindle); "pieces" lists every assembled piece and its carried coordinate systems. Lengths in mm. |
| `set_tool_body` | `axis?`, `path`, `tip_offset?`, `tool` | Give a milling tool (or a boring bar on a mill) a body from a holder or assembly file (STEP, STL, OBJ), placed along the spindle axis. With axis and tip_offset: the model direction that points from the tip toward the spindle, and the model origin's height above the tip along it. With neither: a STEP is aligned by the ISO 13399 tool coordinate systems it names, and refused by name when it names none. The collision laws then judge the body's revolved envelope instead of the holder cylinder. Refused by name: a lathe-held tool (use set_lathe_tool_body), a body reaching into the flutes, a mesh that is no body, a model too detailed to import at full fidelity. One undoable step. |
| `set_lathe_tool_body` | `along`, `insert_zone?`, `path`, `radial`, `tip?`, `tool` | Give a lathe-held tool (turning, grooving, threading or form insert, or a boring bar) a holder body from a file (STEP, STL, OBJ), placed in the turning tool frame: radial is the model direction that points away from the spindle axis, along the model direction of the lathe's +Z (chuck toward the free end), tip the model point the moves carry (the insert's nose centre). The body need not be symmetric: every move of a turning operation is then judged against the part and the standing stock, a rub blocking the post. insert_zone (optional) is a box about the tip, in that frame, holding the insert plate the file models - the judge leaves it out. Refused by name: a tool that is no lathe steel, directions that are not square, a tip far from the body, a zone larger than one insert. One undoable step. |
| `attach_tool_body_piece` | `along?`, `axis?`, `path`, `piece_csys?`, `radial?`, `target_csys?`, `target_piece?`, `tip?`, `tip_offset?`, `tool` | Attach a modular holder/adapter/clamping-unit piece (STEP, STL, OBJ) onto a tool's existing body as one undoable step. With no explicit placement arguments, mates by unambiguous ISO 13399 MCS <-> CSW coordinate systems (or pass target_piece / target_csys / piece_csys to pick the pair, axis + tip_offset for spindle placement, or radial + along + optional tip for lathe placement). Combined pieces are judged and displayed together. |
| `remove_tool_body_piece` | `index`, `tool` | Remove piece at 0-based index from a multi-piece tool body assembly and rebuild its collision envelope as one undoable step. Refused by name when index is out of range or only one piece remains (use clear_tool_body to remove the whole body). |
| `set_lathe_insert_zone` | `insert_zone`, `tool` | Set or clear (insert_zone: null) the insert zone of a tool's lathe body, keeping its mesh and placement: a box about the tip, in the turning tool frame (x radial, y normal, z along the spindle), holding the insert plate - lo at or below 0 and hi at or above 0 on every axis, no farther from the tip than one insert reaches. One undoable step. |
| `clear_tool_body` | `tool` | Remove a tool's modelled body (either frame): the holder cylinder is judged again, and a turning tool's holder is no longer judged (its operations say so). One undoable step. |
| `add_fixture_plate` | `counterbore?`, `dimensions?`, `dowels?`, `on_table?`, `position?`, `preset`, `rotation?`, `setup?`, `thread?` | Place a built-in generic grid (tooling) plate as a fixture of a setup - the active one by default. Its frame's origin is the plate's corner on its TOP face (x along the length, y along the width, the slab below). Grid locations: rows lettered along +Y from A, columns numbered along +X from 1 (A1 nearest the origin corner). Either lay it centred on the machine's table (on_table) or give a position/rotation. Optional overrides in mm, thread, dowel pattern and counterbore. The collision mesh is a solid slab. One undoable step; nonsense figures are refused by name. |
| `set_fixture_plate` | `counterbore?`, `dimensions?`, `dowels?`, `name`, `thread?` | Change a placed built-in plate's figures (dimensions, thread, dowels, counterbore). The mesh is regenerated and every fixture on it is re-placed at its named location (refused if a location is gone, a fixture would hang off, or a mod vise jaw would reach into the stock); `warning` names a re-placed fixture or the new slab sitting in a part or the stock, or a mod vise jaw lifted off the stock. One undoable step. |
| `place_on_plate` | `dowels?`, `fixture`, `hole?`, `plate`, `yaw?` | Place a fixture (a built-in vise, an imported fixture, another plate) on a plate: at a grid hole ("C3": its frame's origin on the hole at the plate top) or on a dowel pair (["A1","A3"]: origin on the first, +X toward the second), turned yaw degrees about the plate's Z. The place is remembered: moving the plate moves it. A rotary subplate goes only on a dowel pair as far apart as its pin bores (#821). Refused by name: an unknown location, a fixture hanging off the plate, a subplate's pins that do not fit. One undoable step. |
| `detect_plate_grid` | `clear?`, `name` | Make an imported fixture a plate by detecting its hole grid (the Detect holes rule, read in the model's own frame: holes on its Z, an axis-aligned lattice, each hole snapped to its node within 0.05 mm; a plate turned in its model is refused). Refused by name when its holes form no regular grid. clear: true stops it being a plate. One undoable step. |
| `get_plate_grid` | `name` | Read a plate's grid: pitch, rows and columns, the location names, gaps, the dowel lattice, and the fixtures standing on it. |
| `add_mod_vise_pair` | `adjustable?`, `fixed?`, `hole`, `insert?`, `plate`, `size`, `yaw?` | Place a modular plate-mounted vise on a fixture plate: two jaw blocks, each bolted to grid holes. The FIXED block goes on `hole` (its anchor bolt), turned `yaw` (0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees; at 0 its jaw faces the plate's +Y). The ADJUSTABLE block, turned half a turn, goes on the same grid line at the hole nearest the setup's stock that leaves it clear, then slides along its slots until its jaw touches the stock. Refused by name: stock out of the slots' reach, a block off the plate, a plate with no grid, no stock, stock in the fixed jaw or beside the jaws. Generic preset sizes with optional overrides (mm); both blocks ride the plate. One undoable step. |
| `set_mod_jaw` | `figures?`, `insert?`, `name` | Change a placed mod vise jaw block's figures (mm) or its jaw inserts; an adjustable block's `slide` too. The block stays on its hole and turn and its solid is regenerated. Refused by name: not a jaw block, a figure that breaks the block law, a bolt or pin off the grid where it stands, the block hanging off its plate, its jaw face pushed into the stock. A jaw lifted off the stock comes back as `warning`. One undoable step. |
| `refit_mod_vise` | `adjustable`, `fixed?` | Re-fit a mod vise pair's ADJUSTABLE block to the setup's stock as it stands now (after the stock changed): the fixed block stays, the adjustable block moves to the hole nearest the stock that clears it and slides until its jaw touches the stock. `fixed` names its fixed block when its plate carries more than one. Refused by name, with nothing moved: stock out of the slots' reach, stock in the fixed jaw or beside the jaws, no stock. One undoable step. |
| `set_units` | `unit` | Set the document's unit, "mm" or "inch": every number the app shows, and the unit every post writes the program in (G21 / G20, or the control's own word). One undoable step. Refused by name: the unit the document already has, any other word. A post that cannot write inch (the Makera Carvera) refuses an inch document when posting. |
| `fit_stock` | `margin?`, `shape?`, `sides?` | Fit the active setup's stock to its part models, as the Stock page's Fit to Models does: a box (`shape` "box", the default) or a Z cylinder snug about the parts ("cylinder") with `margin` mm on every side (default 2), or a box with `sides` = [-X, +X, -Y, +Y, -Z, +Z] allowances in mm. Only the parts are measured - vises, accessories, plates and tagged fixtures are left out. The stock keeps its rotation, and the fit is made on the stock's own axes (a stock laid along X or Y wraps the parts along its own length). One undoable step; refused by name with no models, a negative allowance or a flat part. |
| `pick_in_box` | `box`, `kind?`, `mode?`, `operation`, `replace?`, `through?` | Box-select features into an operation's picks, seen from straight above (+Z, like the Top view): every visible feature edge chain (kind "chains", the default) or face (kind "faces") whose outline lies inside the world X/Y box (mode "window", the default) or touches it (mode "crossing"). Without "through" the box is visible-only: hidden edges and faces (under the top face) are left out; "through": true takes them too, like the viewport's Pick through toggle. Mesh triangulation edges are never taken. Adds to the current picks unless replace is true. One undo step. |
| `get_rotary_stack` | `setup?` | Read how a setup's rotary is raised (#821): the rotary subplates in the setup and every plate under each (top down, with thicknesses), the setup's stated nose_to_axis if any, and the machine's work-turning rotaries' nose_to_axis - the figures the index-swing check judges with (the stated figure wins; else the machine's less the tallest stack). `refused` names why the check cannot judge (an imported plate with no stated thickness under a subplate, a stated figure that is no length). |
| `set_setup_nose_to_axis` | `nose_to_axis`, `setup` | State a setup's own spindle-nose-to-rotary-centerline figure, mm, measured on the stack the rotary stands on (a subplate on a fixture plate) - it wins over the machine file's figure less the stack. null clears it. One undoable step; a figure that is not a length over zero (or over 5000 mm) is refused. |
| `get_thread_infeed` | `name` | Read a Threading operation's infeed plan, including default values, spring passes and repeat_each_depth. |
| `set_thread_infeed` | `infeed_plan`, `name` | Patch a Threading operation's infeed plan through EditOperationParams. Unspecified fields keep their values. One undo step. Refuses unknown fields and invalid plans by name. |
| `set_workholding_max_rpm` | `max_rpm`, `setup?` | State the rated maximum rpm of a lathe setup's chuck or collet (null clears it). Constant surface speed clamps to the lowest of the machine's, the tool's and this limit (Fanuc G50 S, Tormach G96 D); a constant-rpm turning operation over it is refused by name at the post. One undo step. |
| `set_sheet_job` | `allowance?`, `clamp_clearance?`, `clear?`, `length?`, `thickness?`, `width?`, `xy_zero?`, `z_zero?` | Set up the active setup as a flat-sheet router job, as one undo step: the stock becomes a box of the sheet's length (X), width (Y) and thickness; the WCS moves to Z zero at the sheet top or the spoilboard and XY zero on the stated corner (front_left by default). The through-cut allowance (how far a cut may go into the spoilboard, mm) is required and always stated; the post refuses by name a move below the sheet bottom less the allowance, or a rapid across below the sheet top plus the clamp clearance. {"clear": true} drops only the record. Sizes in mm. |
| `rename_operation` | `name`, `new_name` | Change an operation's display name. Its stable key (what scripts, saved files and other tools address it by) and its place in the program do not change; naming it back to its key clears the display name. Names are unique and cannot take another operation's key. One undo step. |
| `reorder_operation` | `name`, `place?`, `target` | Move an operation before or after another operation of the SAME setup, as the browser's drag and drop does. The order is saved with the project and is the order the program posts, simulates and computes rest material in; moving between setups is refused. Answers with that setup's operations in their new order. One undo step. |
| `mark_operation_reviewed` | `name` | Clear an operation's migration needs-review warning once you have inspected the migrated operation. Refused by name when the operation is not flagged. One undo step. |
| `electrode_from_faces` | `condition?`, `name`, `orbit?`, `picks`, `pickup`, `setup?`, `stub`, `undersize?` | Generate a sinker EDM electrode from the picked faces of a part's cavity - its level floor and every vertical wall standing on it (list_features ids) - and add it as a document tool. The electrode is the cavity's outline offset inward by the undersize (stated in mm, or read from a machine EDM condition by id) plus an optional orbit radius, and stands a stated stub above the cavity's mouth. Answers with the electrode and the burn point, cavity size and heights a Sinker Burn of this cavity states. An axis-aligned rectangular cavity yields a rectangular electrode (shape "rectangle"); any other outline of planar vertical walls yields a body electrode (shape "outline") whose record carries its section, as [x, y] points in mm about the burn point. A face set that is no single cavity is refused by name. One undo step. |
| `edit_machine` | `patch`, `setup?` | Edit the mounted machine's definition with a JSON merge patch (RFC 7396: an object merges, null removes a key, any other value replaces) - e.g. {"edm": {"max_orbit_radius": 0.5, "conditions": [...]}}. Applies as one undoable mount, like the Machine window's Apply. Keys are those get_job's machine.definition shows; unknown keys and every insane value are refused by name, changing nothing. With setup, edits that setup's own machine (it must have one); without, the document's. |
| `set_tool_number` | `number`, `tool` | Give a document tool its controller number (the T.. / H.. a post writes, which must match the machine's tool table). Returns the tool's own number and the number it posts as (get_job's tool rows show both). One undoable step. Refused by name: an unknown or non-tool name, a number outside 1-99999, null, a number another tool already has on the same machine, and a no-op. |
| `export_agie_inspection` | `directory`, `operation` | Export one selected DXF Wire Contour die opening for Classic 2S inspection. The setup uses 10 mm steel, 0.25 mm wire and a 3 mm start hole. Physical stock XY is unknown. Native length and width are zero. Writes a new ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. |
| `create_agie_inspection` | `chain`, `drawing`, `name`, `start`, `tool` | Create one nominal inspection opening on the active Classic 2S setup with a selected DXF chain and 3 mm start hole. No machining condition or capture is assigned. One undo step. |
| `get_post_options` | `setup?` | Read post options (skip_stops, per_op, threading, end_units, smoothing, between_setups, wcs_rotation, explain), resolved per-post script_options, and the target post's script_schema. With setup, reads that declared setup's resolved options and whether it follows the document; without setup, reads the document's. |
| `set_post_options` | `between_setups?`, `end_units?`, `explain?`, `follow?`, `per_op?`, `script_options?`, `setup?`, `skip_stops?`, `smoothing?`, `threading?`, `wcs_rotation?` | Set post options and/or per-post script_options as one undoable step. Target is explicit: with setup, sets that setup's own options or follow: true returns both built-in and script options to following the document; without setup, sets the document's. Pass null inside script_options to reset one key to the script default. Omitted fields keep their current values. |
| `import_dxf` | `join_tol?`, `name?`, `path`, `setup?`, `units?` | Place a DXF drawing (ASCII DXF: LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE, POLYLINE) as a profile on the top face of a setup's stock, at the stock origin - the active setup by default. A profile is reference geometry for cutting, not a model: set_stock first, a setup needs no model. units "mm" or "in" wins over the file's $INSUNITS; a file that states no unit is refused by name until units is given (never guessed). The reply states the units used, the layers, the closed, open and rejected chains, and the skipped entities by kind. One undo step. Refused by name: a setup with no stock, an unknown setup, a file that is not .dxf, a malformed or binary DXF, a drawing with nothing to place, a name in use. |
| `move_dxf_profile` | `angle?`, `name`, `position` | Move a placed DXF profile on the top face of its setup's stock: position [x, y] in mm from the stock origin, and an optional angle in degrees about the face normal, counterclockwise seen from above (omitted keeps the current one). A profile has no Z and no tilt: it stays on the face and moves with the stock. One undo step. Refused by name: an unknown name, a name that is not a DXF profile, a placement that is not finite. |
| `insert_text` | `angle?`, `height`, `letter_spacing?`, `name?`, `position?`, `setup?`, `text` | Place a typed string as a profile of single-line engraving strokes on the top face of a setup's stock - the active setup by default. The strokes are tool-centreline paths in mm on the layer "text", made from CamCraft's own stroke font: capital letters, digits, the space and - _ . : / # + = ( ) only. height is the cap height in mm (0.5 to 1000). position [x, y] is the left end of the baseline in mm from the stock origin (default [0, 0]); angle turns the baseline in degrees about the face normal, counterclockwise seen from above (default 0). letter_spacing adds a gap between characters in mm (default 0). The result is a profile like one from import_dxf: move_dxf_profile moves it, and get_job lists it under "profiles". One undo step. Refused by name: an empty text, a character with no glyph (a lower-case letter is not changed to a capital), a height or spacing outside the limits, a setup with no stock, an unknown setup, a name in use. |
| `import_svg` | `join_tol?`, `name?`, `path`, `setup?`, `units?` | Place an SVG drawing (path, rect, circle, ellipse, line, polyline, polygon; groups with transforms; use of an element in the same file) as a profile on the top face of a setup's stock, at the stock origin - the active setup by default. Like import_dxf: set_stock first, a setup needs no model, move_dxf_profile moves the profile and get_job lists it under "profiles". The file's width and height (mm, cm, in, pt, pc or px at 96 to the inch) and viewBox give the size; Y is flipped so the drawing looks as it does in the editor. A file that states no physical size is refused by name until units ("mm" or "in", the size of one drawing unit) is given (never guessed); a file that states its size refuses units. Circular arcs stay arcs; Beziers and other ellipses become lines within 0.005 mm. Top-level groups are layers (Inkscape label, else id). Text, images, clip paths, masks, styles and references to other files are skipped and counted by kind; fill and stroke are not read. One undo step. Refused by name: a setup with no stock, an unknown setup, a file that is not .svg, malformed XML or path data, a zero or negative size, a degenerate arc, a file larger than the import budget, a drawing with nothing to place, a name in use. |
| `insert_outline_text` | `angle?`, `font`, `height`, `letter_spacing?`, `name?`, `position?`, `setup?`, `text` | Place a typed string in a TrueType outline font as a profile of closed shapes on the top face of a setup's stock - the active setup by default. The shapes take a pocket, a V-carve or a cut-out (insert_text gives single-line engraving strokes instead). font is the path of a .ttf file, or an .otf file with TrueType outlines; the profile keeps the shapes, not the font. height is the font's cap height in mm (0.5 to 1000). position [x, y] is the left end of the baseline in mm from the stock origin (default [0, 0]); angle turns the baseline in degrees about the face normal, counterclockwise seen from above (default 0). letter_spacing adds a gap between characters in mm (default 0). The shapes are lines in mm on the layer "text"; a letter's hole (O, A) is a hole of its shape. move_dxf_profile moves the profile, and get_job lists it under "profiles". One undo step. Refused by name: a font that cannot be read, a font with CFF outlines or a font collection, an empty text, a character the font does not have, outlines that cross or touch, a height or spacing outside the limits, a setup with no stock, an unknown setup, a name in use. |
| `import_tool_holder_dxf` | `path`, `tool`, `units?` | Import a 2D half-profile ASCII DXF (one LINE on layer CENTRELINE plus an open LINE/ARC profile chain wholly on one side) as a tool's revolved holder body. The centreline must be parallel to Y. DXF +Y is tool +Z; z = 0 is the lower end of the centreline, independent of draw direction. One undo step; missing centreline, crossing geometry, closed loops, splines or missing $INSUNITS (unless "units" is stated) refuse by name. |
| `export_tool_holder_dxf` | `path`, `tool` | Export a document tool's holder body or drawn/converted spun profile to an ASCII DXF half-profile in millimetres (layers CENTRELINE and PROFILE, $INSUNITS = 4). |
| `convert_tool_step_to_profile` | `dxf_out_path?`, `step_path`, `tool` | Convert an ISO 13399 aligned STEP holder/body to a conservative outer-envelope half-profile on a document tool (non-revolved features are enveloped, never cut away) and optionally write it as ASCII DXF. Refuses STEP files with missing, degenerate or ambiguous ISO 13399 coordinate systems instead of guessing +Z. One undo step. |
| `save_cut_recipe` | `library?`, `name`, `operation`, `replace?` | Save an operation's settings (its kind, tool, every parameter such as depths, stepdown, feeds, tabs, leads and ramps, and the workpiece material in force) as a named cut recipe in the user's recipe library. Not a document change: no undo step. A name already in the library is refused unless replace is true. |
| `list_cut_recipes` | `library?` | The cut recipes in the user's recipe library: name, operation kind, tool and material of each. |
| `apply_cut_recipe` | `library?`, `name?`, `recipe`, `source?` | Add an operation from a saved cut recipe, on the stock, a model or a placed DXF profile, in the active setup. One undo step removes it. Refused by the recipe's name: a recipe not in the library, a tool no longer in the document, a material the table no longer has or one other than the material in force. Every add_operation check applies. Not generated until generate runs. |
